summary: Document Core-owned automatic BMC promotion for eligible two-host pools

guide.reason: Clarifies the supported automatic two-host BMC case, Host fencing opt-out, recovery behavior, UI status marker and limits; lease and witness are not available.
guide.verification: Focused Core and UI checks plus a real local Controller browser walkthrough with simulated Core replies are recorded in docs/qa/2026-09-24-automatic-bmc-promotion.md. Host-backed browser and physical hardware checks remain open.

api.reason: Additive optional Core report fields PoolPromotionStatus.automatic and PoolTransferStatus.automatic flow through existing POST /api/v1/agent/report inventory.managed.promotion and inventory.managed.transfer and existing GET /api/v1/pools/{id}/members promotion/transfer projections. No new route or request field; older Core omits the field and clients read omission as false. No API version or capability change.
api.verification: python3 -m unittest tests.test_api_contract passed 74 tests; python3 scripts/generate_api.py --check reported current generated references. See docs/qa/2026-09-24-automatic-bmc-promotion.md.

roadmap.reason: The plan files record the BMC-only subset and open lease/witness gates; no published website roadmap page changes in this slice.

state.reason: Core owns the durable poolTransferRecord in pool-peer.json, including its Automatic flag. Controller keeps no automatic decision or pool record; it projects current host reports, which a replacement Controller reads on subsequent reports.
state.record: Nex Core durable poolTransferRecord in pool-peer.json on the candidate host, including the Automatic flag. A fresh Controller reconstructs its display from that host’s subsequent inventory.managed.promotion report; the Controller stores no promotion state.

verification.method: Focused Core and UI tests, real local Controller browser interaction with fixture Core replies, 74 API contract tests, generated reference check, repository privacy check and a passing combined worktree documentation gate are recorded in the QA note. No host-backed browser or physical hardware verification is claimed.
